explanation: Read all 64 source bits from low to high and append them to the result from left to right. Unsigned source shifts preserve the correct behavior for negative bit patterns.
timeComplexity: O(64), or O(w) for w-bit words. Exactly 64 low-bit extractions and shifts are performed.
spaceComplexity: O(1). Only two 64-bit words are retained.
attribution: Original Java implementation and explanation for EPI Practice, based on the displayed public contract and our independently authored C# solution; no upstream reference code adapted.
correctness: After i iterations, result contains the reversed order of the lowest i original bits, while source contains the unprocessed higher bits. Shifting the result and appending source’s low bit preserves this relation. After exactly 64 steps, every bit is reversed; the final cast changes representation, not the bit pattern.
walkthrough: For x=5, bits 0 and 2 are set. Reversal moves them to bits 63 and 61, giving the unsigned pattern 0xA000000000000000. Interpreted as signed long, that same pattern is -6917529027641081856.
edgeCases: All 64 positions are reversed, including leading zeros and the sign bit.
Unsigned shifts prevent sign extension while reading bits.
